rationale: Every illustration must feel 'sangar': dangerous, imposing or awe-inspiring, with the being as the undeniable subject. The owner rejected earlier images that read as an ordinary person, an ordinary animal, an empty landscape, or a calm, cute or decorative portrait. Those outcomes are failures regardless of technical quality.
prompt: ONE original square premium painterly cinematic Mitoloka illustration of Xacio, the half-human half-fish being of Galician river pools. ANATOMY: one adult female human head and upper torso, two eyes, exactly two human arms, completely opaque thick woven long-sleeved bodice fully covering chest and abdomen, seamless fish lower half with one long scaled tail and one broad caudal fin, NO human legs, no lizard tail because that is another variant. MOMENT: Emerge forcefully from the deep pool close to camera, arching the large visible fish tail out across foreground, one hand gripping wet rock and the other extending toward the viewer; intense commanding gaze, neither smiling nor neutral. POWER: No documented physical supernatural powers; ordinary water displaced by swimming tail only. SCALE & CAMERA: extreme low close angle; subject fills frame, natural documented size, never unsupported gigantic. LIGHT & WEATHER: one warm lateral source, deep shadows, crisp rim, physically moving dust/water only. SURFACE: tactile coarse textures, rich walnut/antique-gold palette. SETTING: dark deep pool of the Miño below Castro de Marce, Galician river rocks and shadowed hillfort far back. MOOD: dangerous or awe-inspiring, never ordinary, cute, calm or decorative. HARD CONSTRAINTS: no text, lettering, symbols, logos, border, signature, watermark; no extra heads or limbs; no franchises; no nudity, transparent clothes, blood, wounds or explicit gore; no generic glow aura, neon lines or energy ribbons.
